blocks.text: SYDNEY — Aviation enthusiasts seized their chance to be part of history as the first flight from Australia’s newest airport took off. Western Sydney International Airport, also known as Nancy-Bird Walton Airport, opened for its first commercial flights on Sunday after about eight years of construction and eight decades of planning. The airport’s inaugural flight, a Jetstar service to the Gold Coast on Sunday morning, sold out in 45 minutes. Self-described “aviation geek” Jack Coffey was one of the 188 people who secured a seat.
